JE LEVEL 3 STUDENT WORKBOOK



What you get in this pack
The student book that follows the forty lessons of the Level 3 Teacher Pack: Excavation, Mapping the
Divergence, Justification and Impact organisers, with room to write your own evidence and arguments.
    40 lesson pages: one page for each lesson, in the order of the Teacher Pack.
    10 story opener pages: predictions, Word Fossils and a reading plan for each story.
    4 keepsake pages: Thinking Tools, Thinking Passport, Word Fossil Log and a Thinking
    Paleontologist certificate.
The ten stories are original Jurassic English storybook workbooks. Each one is a separate
printed book of six chapters. No published book is needed.
Credits. Prompts and organisers: drafted with AI assistance and edited under the editorial oversight of
Jurassic English. © 2026 WorldWise Learning. Jurassic English is a brand of WorldWise Learning.

JE LEVEL 3 STUDENT WORKBOOK



Your Thinking Tools
My name: ____________________ Date: __________
1. The CEIW argument

 Part        Name                     The question it answers

 C           Claim                    What do I think, in one clear sentence?

 E           Evidence                 Which exact words in the story show it? (short quotation, chapter number)

 I           Interpretation           What do those words mean, in my own words?

 W           Warrant                  Why does this evidence prove my claim? So what?

2. Accountable Talk moves

 Move                             What I say

 Marking                          “That is an important idea because…”

 Pressing                         “What in the story makes you say that?”

 Extending                        “I would add that…” / “Another example is…”

3. B1 interpretive markers: suggests that… · implies… · the underlying assumption is…
4. Regulation before reasoning. Before hard thinking, settle your body: Cool Down Pass, the
Butterfly Hug (cross your arms, tap left and right, breathe slowly), or bilateral tapping. Tick the box at
the top of each page when you have done it.
The routine that helps me most is: ______________________________

Lesson 1 · The independent CEIW paragraph
My name: ____________________ Date: __________
☐ Butterfly Hug ☐ Cool Down Pass ☐ Bilateral tapping (tick what you used before you started)
Before the first story: write your first independent CEIW paragraph on the prompt.
The prompt: A town removes every sad song, story and photograph so that nobody is ever unhappy. Is
this a good idea?
CLAIM




EVIDENCE (a fact, an example, or a short quotation from chapter 1 of The Song They Took Out, with
the chapter)




INTERPRETATION (use: suggests that / implies)




WARRANT (the So what?)
